findings.text: In its first paragraph a newcomer learns what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. This covers "what is it" and "why it matters" right away.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The next step is concrete. It lists prerequisites, the clone and setup commands, and a first command to try, and a link in the header jumps straight to it.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: This is Athena's home URL, but the title and almost all of the page are about a different project, firstmate. A newcomer who came for Athena may at first think they are on the wrong site, until the second lede paragraph explains that the page is a demonstration.
findings.source: Title: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: Athena's main promises (a second model checks the work, cost is recorded, a verdict is given) are only stated. The page never shows an Athena run or an example commit. The firstmate study shows that Athena can read code, not the request-to-commit workflow the lede sells.
findings.source: "get back a commit they can trace to the request, the models, the cost and the verdict"

findings.text: This link speaks to the site owner, not the visitor. Placed in the header, it will confuse a newcomer who has no proposals to decide on.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The Counters section points to transition ids that are only defined in the next section. Also, the States list shows only names and tags, so the reader has to go to the Glossary to learn what each state means.
findings.source: Counters: "places-held, changed by transitions t1, t3, t4, t9, t11"

findings.text: The transition cards are dense, use a lot of jargon (yolo, captain, place, secondmate) and repeat hedges like "The cited text states no...". Someone who just wants a feel for Athena will likely skim or skip them.
findings.source: t4 Guard: "worktree clean and committed work landed, whether the captain approved the merge, firstmate merged it under yolo, or a local-only ship landed by a guarded fast-forward; ..."

findings.text: Being open about limits builds trust. But this note describes how the study was made, which means little to a newcomer, and it could make them doubt the study's quality.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f3: "A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths"

findings.text: This section describes repository internals that a first-time visitor cannot use.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"
